answers.explanation: nslookup is everywhere. dig gives more detail but isn't built into Windows.
`set type=` takes any record type: a, mx, soa, ns, txt, ptr.
`aa` would mean the answering server runs the zone. Without it, it's a cached, non-authoritative answer.
NXDOMAIN: non-existent domain. NOERROR means the name exists, even if there's no record of the type you asked for.
NOERROR plus an empty answer is "no data of that type". The SOA tells the resolver how long to cache that.
`-x` builds the in-addr.arpa name and asks for its PTR record for you.
The @ picks the server. Handy for checking whether your own resolver is giving a different answer.
A caching resolver reports how many seconds it will keep the record. When it hits zero, the resolver fetches a fresh copy.
`+trace` makes dig do the iterative lookups itself, so you can watch root, TLD, and authoritative servers answer in turn.
